answer.answer: No. Based on the supplied snapshots, there is no evidence that Iris Build changed its artifact checksum algorithm. Both the earlier snapshot [iris-checksum-old] and the current snapshot [iris-checksum-new] state that Iris Build records SHA-256 checksums for artifacts, so the documented algorithm is identical across both revisions. This also addresses the prior thread's open item on currency: the newest supplied snapshot confirms SHA-256 remains the documented algorithm, so the earlier SHA-256 claim stands as both historically and currently valid. Caveat: the sources only document that SHA-256 checksums are recorded; they do not affirmatively state that no other algorithm was ever used, and they do not address whether additional algorithms are supported.
current_truths: Iris Build records SHA-256 checksums for artifacts, per the current guide snapshot [iris-checksum-new].
historical_truths: Iris Build recorded SHA-256 checksums for artifacts, per the earlier guide snapshot [iris-checksum-old].
The earlier SHA-256 documentation is corroborated rather than superseded by the newer snapshot; no supplied evidence indicates any algorithm change [iris-checksum-old] [iris-checksum-new].

Whether Iris Build supports or records checksum algorithms other than SHA-256 is not addressed by the supplied snapshots.
